doc.name: A — strength training catalogue, workshop bench, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: urethane hex dumbbell pair
Category: strength training
Shot programme: workshop bench
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the art director signing off every frame of this strength training campaign. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the tilted dynamic in a workshop bench treatment.

SUBJECT. A urethane hex dumbbell pair. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Camera rolled into a deliberate tilt with the product on a diagonal. Shoot on a 90mm tilt-shift at f/4, framing for a tight crop that breaks the subject at the frame edge.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a hard fresnel through an egg-crate grid for a crisp-edged shadow. Stage the product on or against cast pigmented resin, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward warm amber highlights rolling into cool slate shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
